parties.relationship: Ledgerline adjudicates medical and dental claims, administers provider payments and prepares and mails member correspondence for Cascade Mutual's commercial and Medicare Advantage lines of business.

sentences.text: This Business Associate Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into as of January 1, 2027 (the "Effective Date") by and between Cascade Mutual Health Plan, a nonprofit mutual health insurer organized under the laws of the State of Washington (the "Plan"), and Ledgerline Claims Services LLC, a Delaware limited liability company ("Business Associate").
WHEREAS, the Plan is a health plan that offers group, individual and Medicare Advantage coverage to residents of Washington, Oregon and Idaho, and is a covered entity under HIPAA.

WHEREAS, under the Administrative Services Agreement between the parties dated as of the Effective Date (the "Services Agreement"), Business Associate adjudicates medical and dental claims, administers provider payment cycles, and prepares and mails correspondence to the Plan's members.
WHEREAS, in performing that work Business Associate creates, receives, maintains and transmits protected health information on the Plan's behalf.
WHEREAS, the Plan is required by 45 CFR 164.308(b) and 164.502(e) to obtain satisfactory assurances from Business Associate in a written contract before permitting it to handle that information.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual promises set out below and other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows.

Each of the following terms, when capitalized in this Agreement, has the meaning given to it in the HIPAA Rules: Breach, Data Aggregation, Designated Record Set, Disclosure, Health Care Operations, Individual, Minimum Necessary, Notice of Privacy Practices, Required By Law, Secretary, Security Incident, Subcontractor, Unsecured Protected Health Information and Use.
"Business Associate" has the meaning given to the term "business associate" in 45 CFR 160.103 and, when used to refer to a party to this Agreement, means Ledgerline Claims Services LLC.
"Plan" means Cascade Mutual Health Plan, which is a "covered entity" as that term is defined in 45 CFR 160.103.
"HIPAA Rules" means the Privacy, Security, Breach Notification and Enforcement Rules at 45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164, as amended from time to time.
"Privacy Rule" means the Standards for Privacy of Individually Identifiable Health Information at 45 CFR Part 160 and Part 164, Subparts A and E.
"Protected Health Information" or "PHI" means protected health information, as defined in 45 CFR 160.103, that Business Associate creates, receives, maintains or transmits on behalf of the Plan.
"Services" means the claims adjudication, provider payment, payment integrity and member correspondence services that Business Associate furnishes to the Plan under the Services Agreement.

blocks.heading: Obligations and Activities of Business Associate

sentences.text: Business Associate shall not use or further disclose PHI other than as permitted or required by this Agreement or as Required By Law.
Business Associate shall implement and maintain appropriate administrative, physical and technical safeguards to prevent any use or disclosure of PHI that this Agreement does not provide for.
With respect to electronic protected health information, Business Associate shall comply with Subpart C of 45 CFR Part 164.

Business Associate shall encrypt PHI at rest and in transit using cryptographic modules validated under FIPS 140 and shall require multi-factor authentication for all remote and privileged access to systems that hold PHI.
Business Associate shall train each workforce member who handles PHI on the requirements of this Agreement before granting that member any system privileges and at least annually thereafter.

Business Associate shall not store, process or view PHI, or permit any other person to do so, from any location outside the United States without the Plan's prior consent, which the Plan may withhold in its sole discretion.
Business Associate shall report to the Plan in writing any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this Agreement of which it becomes aware.
Business Associate shall report to the Plan each Breach of Unsecured Protected Health Information that it discovers, as required by 45 CFR 164.410.
Business Associate shall report to the Plan any Security Incident of which it becomes aware.

The parties acknowledge that pings, port scans, broadcast attacks, denied log-on attempts and similar unsuccessful attempts to penetrate Business Associate's systems occur routinely, and the Plan does not require separate notice of any such attempt that does not result in unauthorized access to PHI.
Business Associate shall mitigate, to the extent practicable, any harmful effect known to it of a use or disclosure of PHI by Business Associate or its agents in violation of this Agreement.
Business Associate shall give notice of each Breach to the Plan's Privacy Officer without unreasonable delay after discovery.
Business Associate shall in all cases deliver notice of a Breach to the Plan no later than ten (10) business days after the Breach is discovered.

A Breach is treated as discovered on the first day on which it is known, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have been known, to any employee, officer or agent of Business Associate other than the person who committed it.

To the extent the information is available, each notice of a Breach shall identify every Individual whose Unsecured Protected Health Information has been, or is reasonably believed to have been, accessed, acquired, used or disclosed.
Business Associate shall furnish the Plan with any other available information that the Plan is required to include in its notification to affected Individuals under 45 CFR 164.404(c).

Business Associate shall cooperate with the Plan's investigation and risk assessment of any Breach and shall not contact affected Individuals, regulators or the media about it unless the Plan directs it to do so.

Business Associate shall reimburse the Plan for the reasonable costs of notifying Individuals, providing credit monitoring and staffing a call center in connection with any Breach caused by Business Associate or its Subcontractors.

Business Associate shall ensure that each Subcontractor that creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI on behalf of Business Associate agrees to the same restrictions, conditions and requirements that apply to Business Associate with respect to that PHI.

Business Associate shall document the commitments of every Subcontractor that handles PHI in a written subcontractor business associate agreement entered into before the Subcontractor first receives PHI.
Business Associate remains responsible to the Plan for the acts and omissions of its Subcontractors with respect to PHI as if they were its own.

Business Associate shall make PHI maintained in a Designated Record Set available to the Plan or, as the Plan directs, to the Individual or the Individual's designee, so that requests for access can be honored.
Business Associate shall act on each request for access forwarded by the Plan within ten (10) business days, in the time and manner that allows the Plan to meet its obligations under 45 CFR 164.524.

If an Individual submits a request concerning his or her PHI directly to Business Associate, Business Associate shall forward the request to the Plan's Privacy Officer and shall not respond to the Individual unless the Plan directs it to.
Business Associate shall make PHI maintained in a Designated Record Set available to the Plan for amendment.
Business Associate shall incorporate into the Designated Record Set any amendment to PHI that the Plan directs or agrees to under 45 CFR 164.526.
Business Associate shall document each disclosure of PHI that it makes and shall maintain the information required for the Plan to provide an Individual with an accounting of disclosures.

Business Associate shall provide the Plan with the information needed to respond to an Individual's request for an accounting of disclosures within fifteen (15) days after the Plan asks for it, consistent with 45 CFR 164.528.

To the extent Business Associate carries out any of the Plan's obligations under Subpart E of 45 CFR Part 164, Business Associate shall comply with the requirements of Subpart E that apply to the Plan in the performance of those obligations.
The parties acknowledge that the Services include mailing the Plan's Notice of Privacy Practices to newly enrolled members and processing member requests for confidential communications.

Business Associate shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to the use and disclosure of PHI available to the Secretary for purposes of determining the Plan's compliance with the HIPAA Rules.
Business Associate shall promptly tell the Plan of any inquiry, compliance review or investigation by the Office for Civil Rights relating to PHI, unless the law prohibits it from doing so.

blocks.heading: Permitted Uses and Disclosures by Business Associate

sentences.text: Business Associate may use and disclose PHI only as necessary to perform the Services for the Plan under the Services Agreement.
Business Associate may use or disclose PHI as Required By Law.

Business Associate shall limit its uses and disclosures of, and requests for, PHI to the Minimum Necessary, consistent with the Plan's minimum necessary policies and procedures as provided to Business Associate.

Business Associate may not use or disclose PHI in any manner that would violate Subpart E of 45 CFR Part 164 if done by the Plan, except for the uses and disclosures for Business Associate's management and administration and for Data Aggregation that this Article permits.
Business Associate may use PHI for its proper management and administration or to carry out its legal responsibilities.

Business Associate may disclose PHI for its proper management and administration or to carry out its legal responsibilities if the disclosure is Required By Law, or if Business Associate first obtains reasonable assurances from the recipient that the information will be held confidentially, further disclosed only as Required By Law or for the purpose for which it was disclosed to the recipient, and that the recipient will tell Business Associate of any instance in which the confidentiality of the information has been compromised.
Business Associate may provide Data Aggregation services relating to the Health Care Operations of the Plan with the Plan's prior approval.
Business Associate may not de-identify PHI, or use or disclose information de-identified from PHI, for any purpose other than performing the Services, unless the Plan has given its prior consent.

The Plan shall notify Business Associate of any limitation in the Plan's Notice of Privacy Practices under 45 CFR 164.520, to the extent the limitation may affect Business Associate's use or disclosure of PHI.

The Plan shall notify Business Associate of any change in, or revocation of, an Individual's permission to use or disclose PHI, to the extent the change may affect Business Associate's use or disclosure of PHI.

The Plan shall notify Business Associate of any restriction on the use or disclosure of PHI that the Plan has agreed to or must honor under 45 CFR 164.522, to the extent the restriction may affect Business Associate's use or disclosure of PHI.

The Plan shall not ask Business Associate to use or disclose PHI in any manner that the Privacy Rule would forbid the Plan itself to use or disclose it, apart from the management, administration and Data Aggregation activities that this Agreement allows.
This Agreement takes effect on the Effective Date and remains in force for as long as the Services Agreement remains in force, unless it is terminated earlier in accordance with its terms.

The Plan may terminate this Agreement and the Services Agreement if the Plan determines that Business Associate has violated a material term of this Agreement and Business Associate has not cured the violation within thirty (30) days after written notice from the Plan.
If the Plan determines that Business Associate has violated this Agreement and that termination is not feasible, the Plan may report the problem to the Secretary.

Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason, Business Associate shall return to the Plan or, at the Plan's election, destroy all PHI that Business Associate or its Subcontractors still maintain in any form.

Business Associate shall retain no copies of PHI after termination, except that where Business Associate demonstrates that returning or destroying particular PHI is infeasible, Business Associate shall extend the protections of this Agreement to that PHI and limit its further uses and disclosures to the purposes that make return or destruction infeasible, for so long as Business Associate maintains it.
Business Associate shall certify the return or destruction of PHI to the Plan in a writing signed by an officer within thirty (30) days after it is completed.
At the Plan's request, Business Associate shall transmit PHI to a successor administrator designated by the Plan in an industry-standard electronic format.
The rights and obligations of the parties under this Article survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement.
A reference in this Agreement to a section of the HIPAA Rules refers to that section as in effect or as amended at the relevant time.
The parties shall take such action as is necessary to amend this Agreement from time to time so that it continues to satisfy the HIPAA Rules and other applicable law.
No other amendment of this Agreement is effective unless it is in a writing signed by both parties.
Any ambiguity in this Agreement shall be resolved in favor of a meaning that permits the parties to comply with the HIPAA Rules.
This Agreement supplements the Services Agreement, and if the two conflict on any matter involving PHI, this Agreement controls.

Business Associate shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Plan and its directors, officers and employees from and against all losses, civil money penalties, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from Business Associate's breach of this Agreement or its negligent handling of PHI.

Business Associate shall maintain cyber liability and privacy insurance with limits of not less than $10,000,000 per claim and in the aggregate throughout the term of this Agreement and for three years thereafter.

Business Associate acknowledges that its breach of this Agreement may cause the Plan irreparable harm for which money damages would be inadequate, and that the Plan is entitled to seek injunctive relief in addition to any other remedy available at law or in equity.
Nothing in this Agreement confers any rights or remedies on any person other than the parties and their respective successors and permitted assigns.
This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Washington, without regard to its conflict of laws rules, except to the extent federal law governs.

Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered to the Plan's Privacy Officer at 1200 Fifth Avenue, Suite 1800, Seattle, Washington 98101, or to Business Associate's Chief Compliance Officer at 4400 Riverside Parkway, Boise, Idaho 83702.
This Agreement may be executed in counterparts, including by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together form one instrument.
IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have caused this Agreement to be executed by their duly authorized representatives as of the Effective Date.
CASCADE MUTUAL HEALTH PLAN, by Margaret Okafor, Senior Vice President and Chief Privacy Officer, dated December 12, 2026
LEDGERLINE CLAIMS SERVICES LLC, by Daniel Reyes, President and Chief Executive Officer, dated December 15, 2026

sentences.text: This Master Services Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into as of January 1, 2027 (the "Effective Date") between Ledgerline Claims Services LLC, a Delaware limited liability company with offices at 4400 Riverside Parkway, Boise, Idaho 83702 ("Ledgerline"), and Cascade Mutual Health Plan, a Washington nonprofit mutual corporation with offices at 1200 Fifth Avenue, Suite 1800, Seattle, Washington 98101 ("Customer").

Ledgerline provides third-party claims administration and member correspondence services to health plans, and Customer wishes to engage Ledgerline to provide those services for its commercial and Medicare Advantage lines of business on the terms below.

"Affiliate" means any entity that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where control means ownership of more than fifty percent of the voting interests of the entity.

"Applicable Law" means all federal and state statutes, regulations and binding agency guidance that apply to a party's performance under this Agreement, including HIPAA and state insurance and prompt-pay laws.
"Breach" has the meaning given in 45 CFR 164.402.
"Customer Data" means all data, including PHI, that Customer or its Members provide to Ledgerline, or that Ledgerline creates or receives on Customer's behalf, in connection with the Services.
"De-identified Data" means Customer Data that has been de-identified in accordance with 45 CFR 164.514(a) through (c).
"Designated Record Set" has the meaning given in 45 CFR 164.501.
"Fees" means the amounts payable by Customer for the Services as set out in each Statement of Work.

"HIPAA" means the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996, the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act, and their implementing regulations at 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164 (the "HIPAA Rules"), each as amended.
"Member" means an individual enrolled in a health benefit plan that Customer insures or administers.
"PHI" means protected health information, as defined in 45 CFR 160.103, that Ledgerline creates, receives, maintains or transmits on Customer's behalf.
"Secretary" means the Secretary of the United States Department of Health and Human Services or the Secretary's designee.
"Security Incident" has the meaning given in 45 CFR 164.304.
"Services" means the claims intake, adjudication, payment, recovery and Member correspondence services described in each Statement of Work.
"Statement of Work" or "SOW" means a statement of work that references this Agreement and is signed by authorized representatives of both parties, the first of which is designated SOW-01.

"Subcontractor" means any third party, including a Ledgerline Affiliate, to which Ledgerline delegates a function, activity or service under this Agreement and which creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI in doing so.

"Unsecured PHI" means PHI that is not rendered unusable, unreadable or indecipherable to unauthorized persons through a technology or methodology specified by the Secretary in guidance issued under section 13402(h)(2) of the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act.
Ledgerline shall perform the Services described in each Statement of Work in accordance with this Agreement.
Each Statement of Work will describe the lines of business, claim types, implementation milestones, service levels and Fees that apply to the Services it covers.
Customer shall provide eligibility files, benefit plan configurations and provider fee schedules in the formats and on the schedule specified in the applicable Statement of Work.
Customer retains sole responsibility for coverage decisions, benefit design, medical necessity determinations and final decisions on Member appeals.
Either party may propose a change to the scope of a Statement of Work, and no change takes effect until both parties sign a change order describing it and any resulting adjustment to the Fees.

If the documents that make up this Agreement conflict, they control in the following order: first, Exhibit A (Business Associate Terms) as to any matter involving PHI; second, the body of this Agreement; third, the applicable Statement of Work; and fourth, any other exhibit or attachment.
As between the parties, Customer owns all Customer Data.
Customer grants Ledgerline a non-exclusive, non-transferable license during the Term to process Customer Data as necessary to provide the Services.
Ledgerline may use and disclose PHI only as necessary to perform the Services described in the applicable Statement of Work.
Ledgerline may create De-identified Data from Customer Data to prepare the benchmarking and cost trend reports described in the applicable Statement of Work.
Ledgerline may retain and analyze De-identified Data for the purpose of improving its claims editing logic, during and after the Term.
Ledgerline shall not attempt to re-identify any De-identified Data or sell De-identified Data to any third party.
Ledgerline shall store and process Customer Data exclusively in data centers located in the continental United States.
Ledgerline shall not permit personnel located outside the United States to view or handle Customer Data without Customer's prior written consent.

Customer shall pay the Fees set out in each Statement of Work, which under SOW-01 consist of a per-member-per-month administrative fee of $4.85 for each commercial Member and $6.10 for each Medicare Advantage Member.
Implementation fees, print-and-postage charges and recovery contingency fees are billed as set out in the applicable Statement of Work.
Ledgerline will invoice Customer monthly in arrears, and Customer shall pay each undisputed invoice within forty-five (45) days after receipt.
Late amounts bear interest at the lesser of one percent per month or the highest rate permitted by law.

Customer may withhold any invoiced amount it disputes in good faith if it gives Ledgerline a written description of the dispute before the due date, and the parties shall work in good faith to resolve the dispute within thirty (30) days.

Beginning on the first anniversary of the Effective Date, Ledgerline may increase the Fees once in each contract year by no more than the lesser of three percent or the annual change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers.
Fees exclude sales, use and similar taxes, which Customer shall pay unless it provides a valid exemption certificate, and each party is responsible for taxes on its own income.

Ledgerline shall adjudicate at least ninety-eight percent of clean claims within fourteen (14) calendar days after receipt and shall maintain financial payment accuracy of at least ninety-nine percent, each measured quarterly.

If Ledgerline misses a service level in any calendar quarter, Customer will receive the service credit specified in the applicable Statement of Work, up to a maximum of ten percent of the Fees for that quarter.
Service credits are Customer's sole monetary remedy for a missed service level but do not limit Customer's other rights under this Agreement.

Ledgerline shall deliver to Customer by the fifteenth day of each month an operations report showing performance against each service level, open claims inventory, and Member correspondence volumes for the prior month.
Ledgerline shall print and mail explanations of benefits, claim denial letters and other Member correspondence using templates that Customer has approved.
Customer is responsible for the content of each approved template, and Ledgerline is responsible for merging the correct Member and claim data into it.

Ledgerline shall make its provider and Member portals available at least 99.5 percent of the time in each calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance announced at least five (5) business days in advance.

Ledgerline shall maintain business continuity and disaster recovery plans for the Services, test them at least annually, and resume claims processing within forty-eight (48) hours after declaring a disaster.
Ledgerline shall maintain internal controls over claims processing and disbursement that are designed to ensure that claims are paid accurately, to the correct payee, and in the correct amount.
Ledgerline shall implement and maintain appropriate administrative, physical and technical safeguards designed to prevent any use or disclosure of Customer Data that this Agreement does not allow.
Ledgerline shall comply with the Security Rule, 45 CFR Part 164, Subpart C, with respect to PHI that it creates, receives, maintains or transmits in electronic form.
Ledgerline's Chief Information Security Officer is responsible for the security of the systems used to provide the Services and is Customer's primary contact on security matters.
Customer shall keep confidential the credentials issued to its personnel for Ledgerline's provider and Member portals and is responsible for activity performed under those credentials.
Ledgerline shall require multi-factor authentication for all remote access and all privileged access to systems that store or process Customer Data.
Ledgerline shall encrypt Customer Data at rest using AES-256 or stronger and in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher.
Ledgerline shall engage an independent firm to perform penetration testing of its claims platform at least annually and shall remediate critical findings within thirty (30) days.
Once in each contract year and at no additional charge, Ledgerline shall give Customer a copy of its most recent SOC 1 Type II report covering claims processing and disbursement controls.
Ledgerline shall give Customer, on the same schedule, its most recent SOC 2 Type II report covering the security, availability and confidentiality trust services criteria.
Ledgerline shall assign qualified personnel to the Services and shall replace any individual whom Customer reasonably asks to be removed from its account.
Ledgerline shall complete criminal background checks on all personnel before giving them access to Customer Data, to the extent Applicable Law permits.

"Confidential Information" means non-public information that one party discloses to the other and that is marked confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential, including the Fees, the terms of each Statement of Work, and Ledgerline's claims editing logic.

The receiving party shall protect the disclosing party's Confidential Information with at least the degree of care it gives its own information of like importance, and never less than reasonable care.

The receiving party may disclose Confidential Information only to its employees, contractors and advisers who need to know it for purposes of this Agreement and who are bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than this Section 7.

Confidential Information excludes information that is or becomes public through no fault of the receiving party, was known to the receiving party without restriction before receipt, or is independently developed without reference to the disclosing party's information.
Customer Data, including PHI, is governed by Section 3 and Exhibit A rather than this Section 7, and any exclusion in Section 7.3 does not apply to PHI.
Ledgerline warrants that it will perform the Services in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with generally accepted claims administration practices.

Ledgerline warrants that it will adjudicate claims in accordance with the benefit plan configurations and fee schedules that Customer provides, and will reprocess any claim it adjudicates incorrectly at no additional charge.
Each party warrants that it has full authority to enter into this Agreement and that its performance under this Agreement will comply with Applicable Law.
EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY STATED IN THIS AGREEMENT, LEDGERLINE MAKES NO OTHER WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING ANY IMPLIED WARRANTY OF MERCHANTABILITY OR FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.

Ledgerline shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its directors, officers and employees from and against third-party claims, regulatory fines and penalties, and related reasonable attorneys' fees to the extent arising from Ledgerline's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of Exhibit A.

Ledgerline shall reimburse Customer for the reasonable costs of notifying affected Members, regulators and the media, and of offering Members twelve months of credit monitoring, following any Breach caused by Ledgerline or its Subcontractors.

Customer shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Ledgerline from and against third-party claims to the extent arising from benefit determinations Customer makes or from inaccurate eligibility data that Customer supplies.

The indemnified party shall give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of any claim, allow it to control the defense and settlement, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE MONTHS BEFORE THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM.
NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, SPECIAL OR PUNITIVE DAMAGES, OR FOR LOST PROFITS, EXCEPT IN CONNECTION WITH EXCLUDED CLAIMS.

"Excluded Claims" means a party's indemnification obligations, a party's gross negligence or willful misconduct, and Ledgerline's breach of Exhibit A, provided that Ledgerline's total liability for breach of Exhibit A is limited to three times the Fees paid in the twelve months before the event giving rise to the claim.

Ledgerline shall maintain, at its own expense, commercial general liability insurance of at least $2,000,000 per occurrence, professional errors and omissions insurance of at least $5,000,000 per claim, crime insurance of at least $5,000,000 covering claim fund disbursements, and cyber liability insurance of at least $10,000,000 per claim.
Ledgerline shall furnish certificates of insurance on request and shall give Customer thirty (30) days' prior written notice of cancellation of any required policy.

This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for an initial term of three years, after which it renews automatically for successive one-year terms unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least one hundred eighty (180) days before the end of the then-current term (the initial term and any renewal terms together, the "Term").

Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work if the other party materially breaches this Agreement, including Exhibit A, and fails to cure the breach within thirty (30) days after receiving written notice describing it.

Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other party becomes insolvent, makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors, or becomes the subject of a bankruptcy proceeding that is not dismissed within sixty (60) days.
Termination of a Statement of Work does not terminate this Agreement or any other Statement of Work.
Customer shall pay all Fees for Services performed through the effective date of termination.

For up to six months after termination or expiration, Ledgerline shall provide reasonable transition assistance at its then-current professional services rates, including run-out claims processing if Customer requests it.
Ledgerline shall deliver Customer Data to Customer or its designated successor administrator in a mutually agreed, industry-standard file format.

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Washington, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles, and the parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in King County, Washington.

Notices under this Agreement must be in writing and are effective on receipt when delivered by hand or by nationally recognized overnight courier to the receiving party's address in the preamble, with a copy of any notice to Ledgerline sent to its General Counsel and a copy of any notice to Customer sent to its Chief Legal Officer.

Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other party's prior written consent, except to a successor in a merger or a sale of substantially all of its assets that assumes this Agreement in writing.
Ledgerline shall identify in each Statement of Work the Subcontractors it uses for print-and-mail fulfillment, check issuance and claims repricing.
Ledgerline remains responsible to Customer for the acts and omissions of its Subcontractors as if they were Ledgerline's own.

Neither party is liable for a delay caused by events beyond its reasonable control, except that a force majeure event does not excuse Ledgerline's obligations under Exhibit A or its availability commitment under Section 5.5.
The parties are independent contractors, and nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or fiduciary relationship between them.

This Agreement, together with its exhibits and each Statement of Work, is the entire agreement of the parties regarding its subject matter and supersedes all prior proposals, understandings and agreements regarding that subject matter.

No modification of this Agreement is effective unless it is in a writing signed by authorized representatives of both parties, and no waiver is effective unless it is in a writing signed by the waiving party.
The parties shall negotiate in good faith any change to Exhibit A that becomes necessary because of a change in the HIPAA Rules.
Sections 3, 7, 9, 10 and 12.4, Exhibit A, and any other provision that by its nature is intended to continue, will survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement.
This Agreement may be signed in counterparts and by electronic signature, each of which is an original and all of which together are one instrument.
The parties have signed this Agreement through their authorized representatives as of the Effective Date.
LEDGERLINE CLAIMS SERVICES LLC, by Daniel Reyes, President and Chief Executive Officer
CASCADE MUTUAL HEALTH PLAN, by Margaret Okafor, Senior Vice President and Chief Privacy Officer
This Exhibit A forms part of the Agreement and applies whenever Ledgerline creates, receives, maintains or transmits PHI in providing the Services.
Capitalized terms used in this Exhibit A and not defined in Section 1 of the Agreement have the meanings given in the HIPAA Rules.
For purposes of the HIPAA Rules, Ledgerline is Customer's business associate and Customer is a covered entity.
Ledgerline shall direct all communications to Customer under this Exhibit A to Customer's Privacy Officer by telephone and by email to privacy@cascademutual.org.
Ledgerline shall not use or further disclose PHI other than as permitted or required by the Agreement or as required by law.
Ledgerline may not use or disclose PHI in any manner that would violate Subpart E of 45 CFR Part 164 if done by Customer, except for the uses and disclosures that Section A.3 permits.
Ledgerline may use or disclose PHI as required by law.
Ledgerline shall limit its requests for, and its uses and disclosures of, PHI to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended purpose of each request, use or disclosure.
Ledgerline may use PHI for its proper management and administration or to carry out its legal responsibilities.

Ledgerline may disclose PHI for its proper management and administration or to carry out its legal responsibilities if the disclosure is required by law, or if Ledgerline first obtains reasonable assurances from the recipient that the information will be held confidentially, further disclosed only as required by law or for the purpose for which it was disclosed to the recipient, and that the recipient will tell Ledgerline of any instance in which the confidentiality of the information has been compromised.
Ledgerline may provide data aggregation services relating to Customer's health care operations where a Statement of Work calls for them.
Ledgerline may de-identify PHI in accordance with 45 CFR 164.514(a) through (c), and the resulting De-identified Data is governed by Section 3.2 of the Agreement.
Customer, and not Ledgerline, will decide whether and how Members, regulators and the media are informed of any Breach.
Ledgerline shall report to Customer any use or disclosure of PHI not provided for by this Exhibit A of which Ledgerline becomes aware.
Ledgerline shall report to Customer any Breach of Unsecured PHI, as required by 45 CFR 164.410.
Ledgerline shall report to Customer any Security Incident of which it becomes aware.

The parties acknowledge that unsuccessful attempts to access Ledgerline's systems, such as pings, port scans, broadcast attacks and failed log-on attempts, occur routinely, and Customer does not require separate notice of any such attempt that does not result in unauthorized access to PHI.
Ledgerline shall mitigate, to the extent practicable, any harmful effect known to it of a use or disclosure of PHI by Ledgerline or a Subcontractor in violation of this Exhibit A.
Ledgerline shall give Customer notice of any Breach without unreasonable delay after discovery.
In all cases, Ledgerline shall give Customer notice of a Breach no later than five (5) business days after discovery.

A Breach is treated as discovered on the first day on which it is known, or by exercising reasonable diligence would have been known, to any employee, officer or agent of Ledgerline other than the person who committed it.

To the extent possible, Ledgerline's notice of a Breach shall identify each Member or other individual whose Unsecured PHI has been, or is reasonably believed to have been, accessed, acquired, used or disclosed.

Ledgerline shall provide Customer with any other available information that Customer is required to include in its notification to Members under 45 CFR 164.404(c), as that information becomes available.
Ledgerline shall cooperate with Customer's investigation and risk assessment of any Breach and shall make knowledgeable personnel available to Customer for that purpose.
Ledgerline shall maintain a current list of the Subcontractors that handle PHI and shall provide it to Customer on request.
Ledgerline shall ensure that any Subcontractor agrees to the same restrictions, conditions and requirements that apply to Ledgerline under this Exhibit A with respect to PHI.
Ledgerline shall bind every Subcontractor to its obligations regarding PHI through a written business associate agreement executed before the Subcontractor first receives PHI.
If a Member submits a privacy rights request directly to Ledgerline, Ledgerline shall forward it to Customer's Privacy Officer and shall not respond to the Member except as Customer directs.
Ledgerline shall make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Customer so that Customer can respond to a Member's request for access.
Ledgerline shall respond to each request for access that Customer forwards within ten (10) business days, in a time and manner that permits Customer to meet its obligations under 45 CFR 164.524.
Ledgerline shall make PHI in a Designated Record Set available to Customer for amendment.
Ledgerline shall incorporate any amendment to PHI that Customer directs in accordance with 45 CFR 164.526.
Ledgerline shall document its disclosures of PHI and make available to Customer the information required to provide a Member with an accounting of disclosures.
Ledgerline shall deliver the information needed for an accounting of disclosures within ten (10) business days after Customer's request, consistent with 45 CFR 164.528.
Ledgerline shall designate a privacy officer who is responsible for its performance under this Exhibit A.

To the extent Ledgerline carries out any of Customer's obligations under Subpart E of 45 CFR Part 164, Ledgerline shall comply with the requirements of Subpart E that apply to Customer in the performance of those obligations.
The member correspondence Statement of Work lists the privacy functions, such as mailing Customer's Notice of Privacy Practices to new Members, that Ledgerline handles for Customer.

Ledgerline shall make its internal practices, books and records relating to the use and disclosure of PHI available to the Secretary for purposes of determining Customer's compliance with the HIPAA Rules.

Ledgerline shall tell Customer within five (5) business days after it receives any inquiry or investigation request from the Office for Civil Rights concerning PHI, unless the law prohibits it from doing so.
Customer's rights to terminate the Agreement are set out in Section 12.2 of the Agreement.
Upon termination or expiration of the Agreement, Ledgerline shall return to Customer or, at Customer's election, destroy all PHI that Ledgerline or its Subcontractors still maintain in any form.

Ledgerline shall retain no copies of PHI, except that if Ledgerline shows Customer that returning or destroying specific PHI is infeasible, Ledgerline shall extend the protections of this Exhibit A to that PHI and limit further uses and disclosures of it to the purposes that make return or destruction infeasible, for as long as Ledgerline maintains it.
Ledgerline shall certify the completion of any destruction of PHI in a writing signed by an officer within thirty (30) days after the destruction occurs.
